On this page

Early Music ​

Early music encompasses the musical traditions of the Medieval, Renaissance, and Baroque periods, as well as the repertories and performance practices associated with them.

This section explores composers, works, instruments, recordings, and historical performance practices from the Middle Ages to the eighteenth century.

Periods ​

Medieval ​

Music from the Middle Ages, including sacred and secular repertories from the early medieval period through the fifteenth century.

  • Composers
  • Works
  • Repertories
  • Manuscripts

Renaissance ​

The musical traditions of the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries, including sacred polyphony, secular song, and instrumental music.

  • Composers
  • Works
  • Repertories
  • Instruments

Baroque ​

Music of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, including opera, concerto, sonata, chamber music, and sacred music.

  • Composers
  • Works
  • Instruments
  • Performance practice
